subject: Request: Exception to Private/VPC SLA for Customer-Managed WAN (Calyx)
messages:
From: David Liu <d.liu@calyx-fin.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@calyx-fin.com, Gina Ramos <gina.r@calyx-fin.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Request for SLA carveout for customer-managed WAN

Hi Aditya —

Thanks for the demo last week. We’re close to approving Redwood for a private VPC deployment but Procurement and our CISO have flagged SLA language around uptime and latency. A few facts on our side: our production cluster sits in our colo and traffic to Redwood goes over a customer-managed MPLS/VPN with scheduled maintenance windows and occasional microbursts during inter-data-center failovers.

We want to request that network-induced interruptions and customer-network maintenance windows be excluded from any Redwood uptime SLA or that the credit calculation explicitly excludes customer-network latency spikes. I’m attaching a short request doc and a sample network trace showing a 2.4s tail on a few peaks.

High‑level ask: a 12–18 month limited carveout that recognizes Calyx-managed WAN incidents as shared responsibility. We know this is nonstandard, so we’re open to operational controls (visibility hooks, NOC alerts) rather than a full legal waiver.

Can you loop in legal and security? Please let us know what information you need.

—David
David Liu
Head of Infrastructure, Calyx Financial
[Attachment: calyx_sla_request_20270410.pdf (application/pdf)]
[Attachment: calyx_network_trace.png (image/png)]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Request for SLA carveout for customer-managed WAN

Forwarding Calyx’s request — they’re ready to move but need an exception on SLA attribution for customer-managed network events. They propose a temporary carveout (12–18 months) and are open to operational mitigations.

Quick asks:
- Neha: what telemetry/logging/evidence will you need to validate claims when Calyx says the incident was on their WAN?
- Stephanie: any precedent for adding a network-exclusion clause or a conditional SLA credit cap?
- Laura: ops runbook ideas (hooks, pings, synthetic checks) that would let us detect customer-network vs. Redwood runtime failures without overcommitting support overhead.

I’ll draft a short addendum to keep momentum. Attaching their doc.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request for SLA carveout for customer-managed WAN

Thanks for the ping. A few notes from security/compliance perspective:

- Evidence: we need correlated traces showing (1) client packet loss or latency originating in customer border, (2) Redwood-side metrics proving service was healthy (CPU/GPU, process liveness, request queue depth), and (3) no control-plane events or deployments that could explain the incident. Ideally, a 3‑point correlation with timestamps.
- Time window: carveouts tied to scheduled maintenance windows should be pre-notified with an agreed calendar; ad‑hoc incidents must present a post‑incident RFC with traceroutes and maintenance tickets.
- Auditability: Calyx must provide a read-only feed (SNMP/NetFlow, or export via a monitoring aggregator) for the carveout period, or we reserve the right to deny credit.
- Risk: we can entertain a limited exception but only if we can automate verification; manual investigations at scale are unsustainable.

I’ll review their trace file but initial glance shows the tail might be network-related. We should scope what we can automate (synthetic checks + shared monitoring) vs. what needs legal language.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 12:47:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request for SLA carveout for customer-managed WAN

Team —

Quick take from legal: we can add a conditional 'Customer-Network Exception' clause but must be careful with scope. Suggested language (high level):

"Customer-Network Exception: For Private/VPC deployments where Customer controls the network path between Customer resources and the Redwood ingress point (including but not limited to customer-managed MPLS, VPN, or colo cross-connects), Redwood’s uptime and latency SLAs shall exclude incidents where Customer demonstrates, to Redwood’s reasonable technical satisfaction, that a network event on Customer-managed infrastructure was the proximate cause of the service degradation. Except as expressly stated, this exclusion shall not apply to failures of Redwood-hosted components, control plane, or underwriting third-party cloud providers managed by Redwood."

Operational guardrails: limit exception to two incidents per quarter that can be waived without SLA credit and cap total credits to 10% of monthly invoice while exception is in effect. Also require a joint incident review for any waived credit above that cap.

I’ll prepare a draft addendum and flag the clauses that need Neha’s verification hooks.

-Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 08:55:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request for SLA carveout for customer-managed WAN

Operational suggestions:

1) Lightweight synthetic checks: we can run an egress-anchored ping/HTTP synthetic from a probe in Redwood edge to a customer IP (or a Calyx probe) every 30s and keep a 90-day ring buffer.
2) Automated triage: if Calyx’s probe shows >1% packet loss or RTT spike >500ms and Redwood metrics show healthy workers and low queue, mark incident as "candidate customer-network" with automated evidence bundle (probe logs + Redwood metrics + traceroute).
3) Integration: Calyx must grant a read-only token to their monitoring aggregator (e.g., Prometheus endpoint or Datadog link) scoped to the probe/edge data for verification.
4) Support play: first 2 automated incidents per quarter handled via standard support; anything beyond requires joint RCA and possible SLA credit.

I’ll add the monitoring snippet to the draft addendum. This keeps manual work minimal.

-Laura
Laura Bennett
Product Ops, Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: David Liu <d.liu@calyx-fin.com>, Gina Ramos <gina.r@calyx-fin.com>
Cc: procurement@calyx-fin.com, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 16:40:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request for SLA carveout for customer-managed WAN — proposed path forward

David / Gina —

Thanks again for the clear note and the traces. Internal team reviewed and we can proceed with a limited, conditional carveout. Summary of the proposal:

- Scope: Customer-network events (MPLS/VPN/colo-managed links) can be excluded from uptime/latency SLA calculations when Calyx demonstrates (automated evidence bundle described below) that the customer-managed network was the proximate cause. Exclusion does not cover failures of Redwood-managed infra, control plane, or cloud provider outages.
- Verification: automated evidence bundle = Calyx probe/traceroute + packet-loss/RTT thresholds + Redwood runtime health snapshot. Calyx will provide a read-only monitoring feed or a Calyx-hosted probe endpoint we poll.
- Operational caps: up to two automated incidents per quarter may be categorized as customer-network and handled through normal support (no SLA credit). Beyond that, credits limited to 10% of monthly invoice for the carveout period; any larger credit requires joint RCA and agreement.
- Term: proposed pilot 12 months starting on the signed addendum date, auto-review at month 9.
- Next steps: we attached a draft addendum (redwood_sla_addendum_draft.docx). Please: (1) confirm you can share a read-only probe or monitoring feed, (2) confirm the pilot term, and (3) if acceptable, we’ll route the addendum for signature (DocuSign link included).

If you want a quick 30-min call to walk the technical verification piece, I can set that up with Laura and Neha later this week.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com
